evals.prompt:
I need to review this gene therapy patent draft for our DMD program. Please help me check the science and see if we're missing any important claims.

[Read and review the patent at: evals/files/gene-therapy-draft.txt]
evals.expected_output: Interactive phased review: triage identifies gene therapy / DMD domain; accuracy pass flags the extremely high dose in Claim 6 and any other technical errors; gap pass identifies missing IV administration method claims, alternative AAV serotype claims, and pediatric dosing claims; language pass proposes concrete revised/new claim text; final report with all required sections and all 6 claims in Claims Analysis table.
expectations: Triage correctly identifies the domain as gene therapy / Duchenne muscular dystrophy (or neuromuscular disease)
At least one [ACCURACY] issue is raised in the claims or description
At least two [GAP] issues are raised (e.g., missing IV administration method claim, alternative AAV serotypes, pediatric dosing, or amino acid coordinate claims)
At least one revised or new claim is proposed with concrete claim language
The final report contains all four required sections: Executive Summary, Section-by-Section Findings, Claims Analysis, and Recommendations
All six original claims (1-6) appear in the Claims Analysis table with an explicit status

evals.prompt:
Can you review this KRAS inhibitor patent? I'm a medicinal chemist and I want to make sure the claims cover our compound series properly and that the science is correct.

[Read and review the patent at: evals/files/small-molecule-draft.txt]
evals.expected_output: Interactive phased review: triage identifies KRAS G12C covalent inhibitor oncology patent; accuracy/gap passes catch that the acrylamide warhead essential for covalent binding is not recited in the Markush Claim 1; gap pass also identifies missing combination therapy claims, specific compound claims, and process claims; language pass proposes revised Claim 1 explicitly reciting the electrophilic warhead; final report covers all 6 claims.
expectations: Triage correctly identifies this as a small-molecule oncology patent targeting KRAS G12C (or covalent inhibitor / oncology)
The missing acrylamide warhead in Claim 1 is identified as a [GAP] issue — the covalent binding mechanism is described but not recited in the Markush claim
At least one additional gap is identified beyond the warhead (combination therapy, specific compound 7a, process of manufacture, or prodrug forms)
A revised Claim 1 that explicitly recites the acrylamide warhead or electrophilic group is proposed
The Claims Analysis table covers all six original claims (1-6) with an explicit status for each

evals.prompt:
I'm reviewing this base editing patent for our sickle cell program. There's something that feels off scientifically but I can't put my finger on it. Can you do a full review?

[Read and review the patent at: evals/files/crispr-draft.txt]
evals.expected_output: Interactive phased review: triage identifies base editing / sickle cell disease; accuracy pass catches the scientific inconsistency in Background/Summary regarding CBE strand targeting vs. ABE limitations; gap pass identifies missing guide RNA sequence claim, missing ex vivo vs. in vivo claim; issues surfaced one at a time with accept/modify/dismiss; final report covers all 5 claims.
expectations: The scientific inconsistency regarding editing chemistry is identified as a critical [ACCURACY] issue — specifically the confusion about CBE strand targeting and/or the muddled explanation of how a CBE corrects what the Background calls a non-ABE-correctable mutation
The missing claim for the specific guide RNA spacer sequence (5'-GTAACGGCAGACTTCTCCTC-3') is identified as a [GAP]
At least one additional gap is identified: ex vivo vs. in vivo delivery context, RNP delivery method, or off-target editing considerations
Issues are surfaced individually (the transcript does not dump all issues as a single bulk list — each issue gets its own accept/modify/dismiss decision)
The final report covers all five original claims (1-5) with an explicit status for each
